23	## Step 3: Get the diff
24	
25	An invocation is this /review run; a pass reviews one candidate before any fixes.
26	On first entry, initialize one invocation action list and CYCLES=0. Keep both through re-reviews.
27	
28	Each pass has one direction: collect findings in Steps 3–4.8, approve and apply
29	fixes in Step 5, then choose repeat or final persistence in Step 5.8.
30	Do not edit reviewed source until Step 5. All readers examine the same candidate.
31	
32	Fetch the base branch to avoid false positives from stale local state:
33	
34	```bash
35	git fetch origin <base> --quiet
36	```
37	
38	Compute the merge base, then diff the working tree against that point:
39	
40	```bash
41	DIFF_BASE=$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)
42	/workspace/gstack/bin/gstack-review-log --start review
43	git diff "$DIFF_BASE"
44	```
45	
46	1. Save the printed REVIEW_START for this core candidate before reading its diff.
47	2. Each re-review captures a new token before reading, never at log time. Earlier
48	   core tokens remain unused; Step 5.8 finishes only the final core token.
49	3. Native/outside reviewer attempts own separate PASS_START tokens, not REVIEW_START.
50	4. Read non-ignored untracked source too (`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`);
51	   the captured candidate includes it.
52	
53	Keep the review-record terms separate:
54	
55	| Value | Purpose and owner |
56	|---|---|
57	| REVIEW_START / PASS_START | Opaque start receipts from the logger: one for the core pass, one for each other reviewer attempt. |
58	| Finding fingerprint | Groups duplicate findings. The installed helper computes shared-code fingerprints; a matching key alone never proves a prior Skip is reusable. |
59	| `review_binding` | The logger's proof tying a finished review to its captured candidate, not a finding identifier. |
60	| `snapshot_covered_paths` | Supporting advice files the logger proved byte-identical to that candidate. Used by the prior-Skip checker, never supplied by the reviewer. |
61	
62	## Step 4: Critical pass (core review)
63	
64	Select QA surfaces and load their methods below before static review.
65	Step 4 is read-only; Step 4.7 owns setup, charters and probes.
66	
67	From the installed /review SKILL.md's directory, choose one path:
68	- If the caller directory is `review`, Read `../qa/sections/scope.md` in full.
69	- If the caller directory is prefixed `gstack-review`, use `../gstack-qa/sections/scope.md` instead and read it in full.
70	- If neither layout applies, report an unresolved QA installation as a setup blocker; do not guess another path.
71	Use this host's installation, never the product tree. If missing or unreadable, report a QA setup blocker and its affected probes as blocked; continue other safe probes (independent functional/static checks). Missing/unreadable assets block required QA.
72	
73	Use scope's target-selection rules now to choose functional, browser or mixed
74	surfaces from the request and diff. Record that selection before loading methods.
75	Do not execute setup or probes in this read-only step; Step 4.7 owns those actions.
76	
77	Resolve later QA paths in that installed QA directory.
78	> **STOP.** Read `sections/exploratory.md` in that QA installation and the selected methods below before continuing.
79	> A plan command is a probe, not an exception to this gate.
80	**Functional surfaces:**
81	Read `sections/system-functional.md` in full.
82	
83	**Browser surfaces only:**
84	Read `sections/qa-patterns.md` in full.
85	
86	Caller/report templates cannot replace these method Reads.
87	
88	Apply both checklist passes in order: CRITICAL, then INFORMATIONAL. Respect its suppressions.
89	
90	**Enum & Value Completeness requires reading code OUTSIDE the diff.** When the diff introduces a new enum value, status, tier, or type constant, use Grep to find all files that reference sibling values, then Read those files to check if the new value is handled. Shared-code analysis also requires reading related callers outside the diff; keep findings anchored to changed code.
91	
92	**Search-before-recommending:** Research proposed fixes through Aside, especially
93	concurrency, caching, auth and framework behavior:
94	- Check current best practice for the installed framework version.
95	- Look for a newer built-in before proposing a workaround.
96	- Verify API signatures against current docs.
97	
98	```bash
99	_EG="/workspace/gstack/bin/gstack-egress-lib.sh"; [ -r "$_EG" ] && . "$_EG"; _aside_exec() { if command -v _gstack_egress_run >/dev/null 2>&1; then _gstack_egress_run open aside-agent aside.com aside-exec "user invoked this skill" --no-payload aside exec "$@"; else aside exec "$@"; fi; }
100	_aside_exec "Search the web for {framework} {version} {pattern} current best practice and whether a built-in replaces it. Read-only: do not sign in, submit, or change anything. Reply with up to 5 bullets, each with its source URL, then stop."
101	```
102	
103	Without Aside `READY`, use WebSearch if available; with neither, disclose the gap
104	and use existing knowledge.
105	
106	### Shared-code opportunities (core pass)
107	
108	Run this check on every diff, including fewer than 50 changed lines and hosts without Review Army:
109	1. Read the changed code and related unchanged callers using the rubric below. Do not run the standalone history/PR sweep or impose candidate quotas.
110	2. Require at least one verified authored location changed in this diff and at least two actual authored source locations needing the shared behavior. Added or uncommitted source qualifies; invented future callers do not.
111	3. Trace generated copies to authored templates/resolvers. Exclude generated and third-party copies from evidence and savings.
112	
113	### Shared-code evaluation rubric
114	
115	- **Prove the callers.** Require at least two verified, first-party authored source
116	  locations, with functions and lines. Actual added or uncommitted source qualifies.
117	  Only an engineering-plan review may use proposed callers; label those assumptions
118	  and distinguish them from existing source. Similar names or formatting alone do
119	  not establish equivalent behavior. Generated and third-party copies cannot qualify
120	  as callers or contribute savings. Follow generated copies back to authored
121	  templates/resolvers. Existing dependencies remain valid reuse targets.
122	- **Reuse before extracting.** Inspect existing libraries and helpers first. Compare
123	  behavior, inputs, outputs, error handling, side effects, security requirements,
124	  dependencies, and deployment/runtime boundaries. Preserve differences callers need;
125	  do not bridge languages or isolated deployments without a practical shared contract.
126	- **Keep the helper small.** Name its destination and contract, the callers to migrate,
127	  and the smallest adoption sequence. Avoid option-heavy helpers and coupling unrelated
128	  components. Point to existing tests or established use, specify shared-contract and
129	  caller-integration coverage, and describe the blast radius of a shared failure.
130	- **Account for the whole change.** Name removed blocks and their replacements. Show
131	  estimated implementation lines removed, added, and saved separately from total lines
132	  removed, added, and saved including tests and integration. Savings = removed - added.
133	  Count moved code on both sides, exclude generated/vendor lines, use ranges when
134	  uncertain, and do not count overlapping removals twice across opportunities. State
135	  when tests or integration may make the total change grow.
136	- **Rank useful changes.** Favor reliability gains and total net savings, then low
137	  adoption and testing risk. Prefer proven code used by several callers. Use recent
138	  activity to break ties between comparable benefits, not as evidence by itself.
139	  Explain choices centered on older code. Reject similarities with incompatible
140	  contracts and opportunities whose benefits do not justify the abstraction.
141	
142	The core pass owns optional extraction advice. Zero proposals is valid; prefer a compatible existing helper.
143	- Show the changed anchor, verified callers, smallest helper/destination, preserved differences, compatibility tests and shared-failure risk.
144	- Estimate implementation and total removed/added/saved lines from named blocks; deduplicate equivalent proposals and overlapping savings.
145	- Use `"category":"shared-libs","severity":"INFORMATIONAL","advisory":true`, `evidence_paths` (all authored supporting paths) and `helper_target:{"path":"...","symbol":"..."}`.
146	- Include an existing helper's authored path in `evidence_paths` so its contract and raw bytes participate in revalidation. A not-yet-created helper belongs only in `helper_target`.
147	
148	**Identity before merge or suppression:** Use installed `sharedLibsFingerprint`, never model-generated hashes. Send literal JSON on stdin (actual paths/symbol; keep the quoted delimiter), not interpolated shell code:
149	
150	```bash
151	GSTACK_SHARED_LIB=/workspace/gstack/lib/review-evidence.ts
152	bun -e 'const { sharedLibsFingerprint } = await import(process.argv[1]); const value = sharedLibsFingerprint(JSON.parse(await Bun.stdin.text())); if (!value) process.exit(1); console.log(value);' "$GSTACK_SHARED_LIB" <<'GSTACK_SHARED_LIBS_JSON'
153	{"evidence_paths":["src/caller-a.ts","src/caller-b.ts"],"helper_target":{"path":"src/shared.ts","symbol":"sharedHelper"}}
154	GSTACK_SHARED_LIBS_JSON
155	```
156	
157	Use the returned fingerprint; malformed/missing metadata requires revalidation. Real defects follow Fix-First independently: advice or a prior Skip cannot suppress, downgrade or replace them, even with a shared supplied fingerprint.
158	
159	Core findings use the confidence gates below; Step 4.6 applies its specialist gates.
160	Use CRITICAL/INFORMATIONAL labels in the finding format.
161	Step 5.8 combines these finding lines with the checklist's action groups.
162	
163	### Step 4.6: Collect and merge findings
164	
165	Follow these stages in order. Validate core and specialist findings alike, but keep
166	their source labels: specialist scoring is not the final review's defect count.
167	
168	#### 1. Parse outputs
169	
170	After specialist attempts settle, collect their outputs, tagged by actual source.
171	Successful `NO FINDINGS` is a completed empty result. Otherwise parse each JSON line and
172	skip invalid lines. Missing or unusable output is incomplete coverage, not an
173	empty success. Retain each specialist's returned findings for activity stats.
174	
175	#### 2. Validate severity
176	
177	For core and specialist findings with `"severity":"CRITICAL"` and `"advisory":true`,
178	remove `advisory` and retain its `CRITICAL` severity. Treat these as defects before
179	identity, merging, counting, scoring or Fix-First. Never downgrade severity to make
180	advisory metadata consistent. Valid INFORMATIONAL advisories remain advisory in
181	every category, including simplification.
182	
183	#### 3. Identify and merge
184	
185	Partition defects and advisories BEFORE grouping by fingerprint. Never merge a
186	defect with advice, even on a supplied-hash collision. Neither higher-confidence
187	advice nor a prior skipped extraction may replace, downgrade or suppress a defect.
188	
189	Compute identities for both core and specialist findings:
190	- Shared-code advice (category `shared-libs` or fingerprint prefix `shared-libs:`):
191	  call installed `sharedLibsFingerprint` from `/workspace/gstack/lib/review-evidence.ts`
192	  with `evidence_paths` and `helper_target` as literal JSON on stdin, as in the core pass;
193	  never trust a supplied hash or generate one yourself. Missing/malformed metadata
194	  cannot deduplicate or reuse a saved decision.
195	- Other findings: use supplied `fingerprint`, else `{path}:{line}:{category}`
196	  or `{path}:{category}` when no line exists.
197	
198	Within the specialist list, merge matching identities in the same partition: keep
199	the highest confidence and all source names. Confirmation by distinct specialists
200	adds +1 (cap at 10) and `MULTI-SPECIALIST CONFIRMED ({specialist1} + {specialist2})`.
201	Core findings never earn a specialist confidence boost. Preserve `advisory`,
202	`evidence_paths` and `helper_target` through every merge.
203	
204	#### 4. Apply specialist confidence gates
205	
206	- Confidence 7+: show normally in the findings output
207	- Confidence 5-6: show with caveat "Medium confidence — verify this is actually an issue"
208	- Confidence 3-4: move to appendix (suppress from main findings)
209	- Confidence 1-2: suppress entirely
210	
211	Core findings keep the core Confidence Calibration gates.
212	
213	#### 5. Score and present specialists
214	
215	Only specialist findings enter this header and `quality_score`; core findings do not.
216	Use the merged NON-advisory specialist findings for both counts and score:
217	`quality_score = max(0, 10 - (critical_count * 2 + informational_count * 0.5))`
218	Cap at 10 and retain for the review-log entry in Step 5.8. These are not final unresolved-defect totals.
219	Validated `"advisory": true` findings from any source are excluded from score,
220	header, unresolved-defect totals and clean-status blockers. Show them separately;
221	they remain ASK-only, never auto-applied. Real defects follow normal Fix-First.
222	
223	```
224	SPECIALIST REVIEW: N findings (X critical, Y informational) from Z specialists
225	
226	[For each finding, in order: CRITICAL first, then INFORMATIONAL, sorted by confidence descending;
227	 advisory findings last, each rendered with an [ADVISORY] label in place of the severity]
228	[SEVERITY] (confidence: N/10, specialist: name) path:line — summary
229	  Fix: recommended fix
230	  [If MULTI-SPECIALIST CONFIRMED: show confirmation note]
231	
232	PR Quality Score: X/10
233	```
234	
235	**Simplification footer (after the score line):**
236	- If the simplification specialist was dispatched and returned findings, sum
237	  their `lines_removable` values and print: `net: -N lines possible` (omit
238	  findings without the field from the sum).
239	- If it was dispatched and returned NO FINDINGS, print:
240	  `Simplification: lean already — nothing to cut.`
241	- If it was not dispatched, print neither line.
242	
243	Do not add core shared-code savings to this specialist footer. Explain any overlap once in the core proposal instead of presenting duplicate savings.
244	
245	#### 6. Save specialist activity
246	
247	Compile a `specialists` object for the review-log entry in Step 5.8.
248	For DIFF_LINES < 50, keep `specialists: {}`; do not manufacture per-specialist scope records. Otherwise record each considered specialist (testing, maintainability, security, performance, data-migration, api-contract, design, simplification, red-team):
249	- If dispatched: `{"dispatched": true, "findings": N, "critical": N, "informational": N}`
250	- If skipped by scope: `{"dispatched": false, "reason": "scope"}`
251	- If skipped by gating: `{"dispatched": false, "reason": "gated"}`
252	- If not applicable (e.g., red-team not activated): omit from the object
253	
254	Count only findings that specialist actually returned, before deduplication.
255	Advisory findings COUNT in the stats `findings` field, not its defect counts.
256	Include Design despite its different checklist. Preserve dispatch/failure status:
257	zero returned findings from a failed attempt is not a clean review.
258	
259	#### 7. Hand off to Fix-First
260	
261	Send these findings to Step 5 Fix-First alongside the CRITICAL pass findings from Step 4.
262	Consolidate equivalent shared-code advice under the core proposal, retaining all
263	sources and counting overlapping savings once. Keep actual specialist stats;
264	core-only advice must not create a specialist dispatch or finding.
265	Normal AUTO-FIX/ASK rules apply, with advice ASK-only. Missing coverage still blocks
266	completion. Advice never permits edits while readers are active or replaces a required review.
267	
268	---
269	
270	
271	
272	## Step 5: Fix-First Review
273	
274	Before edits, confirm every dispatched reader has returned or is confirmed stopped.
275	For an active or unknown reader/writer, wait or confirm it is stopped. If settlement
276	cannot be confirmed, persist incomplete at Step 5.8 and STOP without edits.
277	Terminal failure does not block fixes from independent evidence. Missing required
278	output still makes the pass incomplete, even after the reader is stopped.
279	
280	Combine core, specialist, Step 4.7 QA, Step 4.8 adversarial and VALID & ACTIONABLE Greptile findings.
281	For QA findings, assign confidence (1–10) from replay/code evidence using Confidence
282	Calibration; retain Step 4.7's severity, not a severity inferred from confidence.
283	Run Step 5.0 severity/prior-skip dedup on all
284	findings before Step 5a classification. Then action every remaining finding.
285	Structured approval does not waive advisory/test_stub ASK gates.
286	
287	### Step 5.0: Cross-review finding dedup
288	
289	**Validate advisory severity first.** If a current finding has `"severity":"CRITICAL"` and `"advisory":true`, remove `advisory` and retain its `CRITICAL` severity. Handle it as a normal defect before suppression, classification, counting, scoring, and persistence. Never downgrade severity to make advisory metadata consistent. Valid INFORMATIONAL advisories remain advisory in every category, including simplification. A prior saved finding with contradictory CRITICAL/advisory metadata cannot establish a skipped defect or advisory decision: exclude it from reuse and revalidate the current finding.
290	
291	Before classifying findings, check this branch's prior user skips.
292	
293	```bash
294	/workspace/gstack/bin/gstack-review-read
295	```
296	
297	Parse only lines BEFORE `---CONFIG---` as JSONL; ignore the non-JSONL footer sections.
298	
299	If no prior reviews exist or none have a `findings` array, skip history matching silently; still classify current findings.
300	
301	**Shared-code advisory decisions use the stricter rule below.** Do not send a
302	finding through the ordinary primary-file rule if its category is `shared-libs`,
303	its fingerprint starts `shared-libs:`, or it has `evidence_paths` / `helper_target`.
304	Missing legacy metadata requires revalidation, not fallback to a line fingerprint.
305	
306	For each JSONL entry that has a `findings` array, for ordinary findings only:
307	1. Collect all fingerprints where `action: "skipped"`
308	2. Note the `commit` field from that entry
309	
310	If skipped fingerprints exist, get the list of files changed since that review:
311	
312	```bash
313	git diff --name-only <prior-review-commit> HEAD
314	```
315	
316	For each finding from Step 4 critical pass, Step 4.5-4.6 specialists and exploratory QA, check:
317	- Does its fingerprint match a previously skipped finding?
318	- Is the finding's file path NOT in the changed-files set?
319	- Is it the same advisory/defect kind? Never use a skipped advisory to suppress a real defect, including a defect with a colliding supplied fingerprint.
320	
321	Suppress only when all conditions hold: the user skipped the same unchanged finding.
322	
323	Matching explicitly skipped shared-code advice requires the complete procedure below.
324	Failed/unknown eligibility requires fresh source review, never ordinary suppression.
325	
326	> **STOP.** Before reusing explicitly skipped shared-code advice (Step 5.0), Read `/workspace/gstack/review/sections/shared-code-reuse.md` and execute it
327	> in full. Do not work from memory — that section is the source of truth for this step.
328	
329	If N > 0, print once: "Suppressed N findings from prior reviews (previously skipped by user)"; do not repeat the items. Otherwise skip the summary.
330	
331	**Only suppress `skipped` findings — never `fixed` or `auto-fixed`** (those might regress and should be re-checked).
332	
333	Count only non-advisory defects in the final summary; list optional advice separately
334	with `[ADVISORY]`. Preserve advisory records and explicit decisions for
335	persistence, but exclude advisories from score penalties, unresolved-defect
336	totals, and clean-status blockers. This does not relax completion, convergence,
337	or missing-reviewer rules.
338	
339	**Keep decisions through fix cycles:**
340	1. Immediately save completed AUTO-FIX/fix and explicit Skip actions in the Step 3
341	   action list, keeping defects separate from advice. For advice retain the helper's
342	   fingerprint, `advisory`, `evidence_paths` and `helper_target`.
343	2. Before reusing a decision, re-read every supporting caller and helper destination,
344	   including secondary callers and transformed/indirect paths. Compare their raw
345	   source with the decision evidence.
346	3. Unrelated auto-fixes do not reopen unchanged identity, contract and tradeoffs.
347	   Material proposal, behavior, migration or risk changes require a new question.
348	   Carrying this invocation's decisions cannot suppress new/recurring defects or
349	   replace Step 5.0's prior-review checker.
350	
351	### Step 5a: Classify each finding
352	
353	For each finding, classify as AUTO-FIX or ASK per the Fix-First Heuristic in
354	checklist.md. Critical findings lean toward ASK; informational findings lean
355	toward AUTO-FIX.
356	
357	**Advisory override:** After severity validation, `advisory:true` is ASK-only. Never auto-apply an optional extraction, even when mechanical. Show `[ADVISORY]`, helper, caller migration, tests and estimated total savings for approval or Skip. Handle real defects independently.
358	
359	**Test stub override:** Any finding that has a `test_stub` field, from a specialist or exploratory QA,
360	is reclassified as ASK regardless of its original classification. When presenting the ASK
361	item, show the proposed test file path and the test code. The user approves or skips the
362	test creation. If approved, follow Step 5d's regression-before-repair order. Derive the test file path from
363	the finding's `path` using project conventions (`spec/` for RSpec, `__tests__/` for
364	Jest/Vitest, `test_` prefix for pytest, `_test.go` suffix for Go). If the test file
365	already exists, append the new test.
366	
367	### Step 5b: Auto-fix all AUTO-FIX items
368	
369	Apply each fix directly. For each one, output a one-line summary:
370	`[AUTO-FIXED] [file:line] Problem → what you did`
371	Retain the completed action in the invocation action list before starting any re-review.
372	
373	### Step 5c: Batch-ask about ASK items
374	
375	If there are ASK items remaining, present them in ONE AskUserQuestion:
376	
377	- List each item with a number, the severity label (or `[ADVISORY]` for optional advice), the problem, and a recommended fix
378	- For each item, provide options: A) Fix as recommended, B) Skip
379	- Include an overall RECOMMENDATION
380	
381	If 3 or fewer ASK items, you may use individual AskUserQuestion calls instead of batching.
382	Retain each explicit Skip choice and its finding metadata in the invocation action list. Do not record an unanswered question as skipped or ask again about a decision already revalidated in this invocation.
383	
384	### Step 5d: Apply user-approved fixes
385	
386	Apply fixes where the user chose "Fix," including Step 1.5's approved TODO changes.
387	Output what was fixed.
388	For an approved defect regression, write the test and prove it fails for the original
389	defect before changing product code. Then require the regression, original probe and
390	adjacent happy path to pass. If that proof cannot run, report the coverage gap and do
391	not claim a verified repair. Healthy uncovered contracts need no invented failing bug.
392	After applying the approved fix, retain its `fixed` action and the original finding metadata in the invocation action list, even if the changed blocks or helper callers are subsequently removed. Approval alone is not a completed fix.
393	After verifying an approved regression and repair, output:
394	`[FIXED + TEST] [file:line] Problem -> fix + test at [test_path]`
395	
396	If no ASK items exist (everything was AUTO-FIX), skip the question entirely.
397	
398	### Verification of claims
399	
400	Before final output, cite the line proving a safety claim, read and cite any
401	handling code you rely on, and name the test file and method for coverage claims.
402	Verify claims or flag them as unknown; "this looks fine" is not evidence.
403	
404	### Greptile comment resolution
405	
406	After outputting your own findings, if Greptile comments were classified in Step 2.5:
407	
408	**Include a Greptile summary in your output header:** `+ N Greptile comments (X valid, Y fixed, Z FP)`
409	
410	Before replying to any comment, run the **Escalation Detection** algorithm from greptile-triage.md to determine whether to use Tier 1 (friendly) or Tier 2 (firm) reply templates.
411	
412	1. **VALID & ACTIONABLE comments:** Use their Step 5a–5d disposition; do not ask a second fix question. Step 5c alone supplies A) Fix / B) Skip for ASK items. After a completed fix, use the **Fix reply template** with diff and explanation; cite the current diff if uncommitted, never invent a commit SHA. A Skip leaves the defect unresolved and grants no new fix permission. If evidence disproves the finding, reclassify it below.
413	
414	2. **FALSE POSITIVE comments:** These are reply decisions, not code approval. Show file:line (or [top-level]), summary, permalink and evidence, then ask:
415	   - A) Reply explaining why this is incorrect (recommended if clearly wrong)
416	   - B) Propose a code change
417	   - C) Ignore — don't reply, don't fix
418	
419	   For A, use the **False Positive reply template** with evidence + suggested re-rank; save to both histories. For B, return to Steps 5c–5d with an ASK proposal. Show the exact change and any `test_stub`; wait for approval before editing. Retain the comment decision so re-entry does not repeat its question.
420	
421	3. **VALID BUT ALREADY FIXED comments:** Reply using the **Already Fixed reply template** from greptile-triage.md — no AskUserQuestion needed:
422	   - Include what was done and the fixing commit SHA
423	   - Save to both per-project and global greptile-history
424	
425	4. **SUPPRESSED comments:** Skip silently — these are known false positives from previous triage.
426	
427	---
428	
429	## Step 5.8: Persist Eng Review result
430	
431	### 1. Re-review after edits
432	
433	1. A pass covers Steps 3–5, including all reviewers before fixes. Allow at most 3 fix cycles:
434	   - Edited: increment CYCLES once. Below 3, repeat Steps 3–5 with a new
435	     REVIEW_START. At 3, persist `converged:false` and remaining findings by filling
436	     and saving the record below. Report nonconvergence and coverage gaps, then STOP
437	     this invocation, without a clean summary or a fourth pass.
438	   - No edits: fill the record below.
439	2. On a repeat, execute Steps 3–5 in order. At Step 4.7, reuse only this invocation's
440	   unchanged-input QA evidence; rerun affected probes after source, test, contract,
441	   command or fixture changes. Reusing a probe never skips a review step.
442	   A probe is affected when its entrypoint, dependencies, contract or replay inputs
443	   change. If impact is uncertain, rerun it.
444	3. **Verify completed actions.** On the final zero-edit pass, reconcile this
445	   invocation's actions with current findings. Deduplicate by structural identity
446	   and advisory/defect kind. For a completed extraction, retain `fixed` and the
447	   original `evidence_paths`/`helper_target`; use `sharedLibsFingerprint` on that
448	   metadata. Verify the replacement helper, remaining callers and tests without
449	   requiring deleted pre-extraction blocks. Current findings determine recurring
450	   defects and unresolved counts; earlier fixes do not suppress them.
451	4. **Recheck skipped advice.** Re-read its final-snapshot supporting source and
452	   reconfirm the decision; otherwise report its history without a reusable skip.
453	   The logger computes `snapshot_covered_paths` from eligible paths whose raw bytes
454	   equal the bound snapshot blobs (`[]` if none). Never carry prior-cycle, supplied
455	   or prior-record coverage forward or build this proof yourself. Fixed advice
456	   needs no skip coverage.
457	
458	### 2. Fill the record
459	
460	- `COMPLETED`: true only when the checklist, dispatched specialists and native
461	  Step 4.8 adversarial pass finish, and every required Step 4.7 probe passes.
462	  Any failed, blocked, inconclusive or not-run required probe means false, as does
463	  a failed native review. `/ship` named-risk acceptance cannot complete `/review`.
464	- `CONVERGED`: true only for a completed zero-edit pass; `CYCLES` counts editing

The same diff can legitimately receive both.

36	## Review Categories
37	
38	### Pass 1 — CRITICAL
39	
40	#### SQL & Data Safety
41	- String interpolation in SQL (even if values are `.to_i`/`.to_f` — use parameterized queries (Rails: sanitize_sql_array/Arel; Node: prepared statements; Python: parameterized queries))
42	- TOCTOU races: check-then-set patterns that should be atomic `WHERE` + `update_all`
43	- Bypassing model validations for direct DB writes (Rails: update_column; Django: QuerySet.update(); Prisma: raw queries)
44	- N+1 queries: Missing eager loading (Rails: .includes(); SQLAlchemy: joinedload(); Prisma: include) for associations used in loops/views
45	
46	#### Race Conditions & Concurrency
47	- Read-check-write without uniqueness constraint or catch duplicate key error and retry (e.g., `where(hash:).first` then `save!` without handling concurrent insert)
48	- find-or-create without unique DB index — concurrent calls can create duplicates
49	- Status transitions that don't use atomic `WHERE old_status = ? UPDATE SET new_status` — concurrent updates can skip or double-apply transitions
50	- Unsafe HTML rendering (Rails: .html_safe/raw(); React: dangerouslySetInnerHTML; Vue: v-html; Django: |safe/mark_safe) on user-controlled data (XSS)
51	
52	#### LLM Output Trust Boundary
53	- LLM-generated values (emails, URLs, names) written to DB or passed to mailers without format validation. Add lightweight guards (`EMAIL_REGEXP`, `URI.parse`, `.strip`) before persisting.
54	- Structured tool output (arrays, hashes) accepted without type/shape checks before database writes.
55	- LLM-generated URLs fetched without allowlist — SSRF risk if URL points to internal network (Python: `urllib.parse.urlparse` → check hostname against blocklist before `requests.get`/`httpx.get`)
56	- LLM output stored in knowledge bases or vector DBs without sanitization — stored prompt injection risk
57	
58	#### Shell Injection (Python-specific)
59	- `subprocess.run()` / `subprocess.call()` / `subprocess.Popen()` with `shell=True` AND f-string/`.format()` interpolation in the command string — use argument arrays instead

61	- `eval()` / `exec()` on LLM-generated code without sandboxing

65	- **Trace it through every consumer.** Read (don't just grep — READ) each file that switches on, filters by, or displays that value. If any consumer doesn't handle the new value, flag it. Common miss: adding a value to the frontend dropdown but the backend model/compute method doesn't persist it.
66	- **Check allowlists/filter arrays.** Search for arrays or `%w[]` lists containing sibling values (e.g., if adding "revise" to tiers, find every `%w[quick lfg mega]` and verify "revise" is included where needed).

72	#### Async/Sync Mixing (Python-specific)
73	- Synchronous `subprocess.run()`, `open()`, `requests.get()` inside `async def` endpoints — blocks the event loop. Use `asyncio.to_thread()`, `aiofiles`, or `httpx.AsyncClient` instead.

84	- CHANGELOG entries that describe changes inaccurately (e.g., "changed from X to Y" when X never existed)

86	#### LLM Prompt Issues
87	- 0-indexed lists in prompts (LLMs reliably return 1-indexed)
88	- Prompt text listing available tools/capabilities that don't match what's actually wired up in the `tool_classes`/`tools` array
89	- Word/token limits stated in multiple places that could drift
90	
91	#### Completeness Gaps
92	- Shortcut implementations where the complete version would cost <30 minutes CC time (e.g., partial enum handling, incomplete error paths, missing edge cases that are straightforward to add)
93	- Options presented with only human-team effort estimates — should show both human and CC+gstack time

98	- Date-key lookups that assume "today" covers 24h — report at 8am PT only sees midnight→8am under today's key
99	- Mismatched time windows between related features — one uses hourly buckets, another uses daily keys for the same data

102	- Values crossing Ruby→JSON→JS boundaries where type could change (numeric vs string) — hash/digest inputs must normalize types

111	- CI/CD workflow changes (`.github/workflows/`): verify build tool versions match project requirements, artifact names/paths are correct, secrets use `${{ secrets.X }}` not hardcoded values

146	## Fix-First Heuristic
147	
148	This heuristic is referenced by both `/review` and `/ship`. It determines whether
149	the agent auto-fixes a finding or asks the user.
150	
151	```
152	AUTO-FIX (agent fixes without asking):     ASK (needs human judgment):
153	├─ Dead code / unused variables            ├─ Security (auth, XSS, injection)
154	├─ N+1 queries (missing eager loading)      ├─ Race conditions
155	├─ Stale comments contradicting code       ├─ Design decisions
156	├─ Magic numbers → named constants         ├─ Large fixes (>20 lines)
157	├─ Missing LLM output validation           ├─ Enum completeness
158	├─ Version/path mismatches                 ├─ Removing functionality
159	├─ Variables assigned but never read       └─ Anything changing user-visible
160	└─ Inline styles, O(n*m) view lookups        behavior
161	```
162

164	without discussion, it's AUTO-FIX. If reasonable engineers could disagree about

3	## Instructions
4	
5	Review the merge-base diff from the caller, including its selected uncommitted and new source. Use the caller's detected base, not a hardcoded branch. Cite `file:line` and suggest fixes. Only flag real problems.
6	
7	**Two-pass review:**
8	- **Pass 1 (CRITICAL):** Run SQL & Data Safety, Race Conditions, LLM Output Trust Boundary, Shell Injection, and Enum Completeness first. Highest severity.
9	- **Pass 2 (INFORMATIONAL):** Run remaining categories below. Lower severity but still actioned.
10	- **Specialist categories (handled by parallel subagents, NOT this checklist):** Test Gaps, Dead Code, Magic Numbers, Conditional Side Effects, Performance & Bundle Impact, Crypto & Entropy, Simplification (unrequested structure). See `review/specialists/` for these.
11	
12	Completeness Gaps and Simplification are orthogonal, not contradictory: Completeness pushes coverage UP (tests, edge cases, error paths), Simplification pushes unrequested structure DOWN (one-implementation abstractions, hand-rolled stdlib, dead flexibility). The same diff can legitimately receive both.
13	
14	All findings get action via Fix-First Review: obvious mechanical fixes are applied automatically,
15	genuinely ambiguous issues are batched into a single user question.
16	
17	**Output format:**
18	
19	```
20	Pre-Landing Review: N issues (X critical, Y informational)
21	
22	**AUTO-FIXED:**
23	- [file:line] Problem → fix applied
24	
25	**NEEDS INPUT:**

27	  Recommended fix: suggested fix

29

31

36	## Review Categories
37	
38	### Pass 1 — CRITICAL
39	
40	#### SQL & Data Safety
41	- String interpolation in SQL (even if values are `.to_i`/`.to_f` — use parameterized queries (Rails: sanitize_sql_array/Arel; Node: prepared statements; Python: parameterized queries))
42	- TOCTOU races: check-then-set patterns that should be atomic `WHERE` + `update_all`
43	- Bypassing model validations for direct DB writes (Rails: update_column; Django: QuerySet.update(); Prisma: raw queries)
44	- N+1 queries: Missing eager loading (Rails: .includes(); SQLAlchemy: joinedload(); Prisma: include) for associations used in loops/views
45	
46	#### Race Conditions & Concurrency
47	- Read-check-write without uniqueness constraint or catch duplicate key error and retry (e.g., `where(hash:).first` then `save!` without handling concurrent insert)
48	- find-or-create without unique DB index — concurrent calls can create duplicates
49	- Status transitions that don't use atomic `WHERE old_status = ? UPDATE SET new_status` — concurrent updates can skip or double-apply transitions
50	- Unsafe HTML rendering (Rails: .html_safe/raw(); React: dangerouslySetInnerHTML; Vue: v-html; Django: |safe/mark_safe) on user-controlled data (XSS)
51	
52	#### LLM Output Trust Boundary
53	- LLM-generated values (emails, URLs, names) written to DB or passed to mailers without format validation. Add lightweight guards (`EMAIL_REGEXP`, `URI.parse`, `.strip`) before persisting.
54	- Structured tool output (arrays, hashes) accepted without type/shape checks before database writes.
55	- LLM-generated URLs fetched without allowlist — SSRF risk if URL points to internal network (Python: `urllib.parse.urlparse` → check hostname against blocklist before `requests.get`/`httpx.get`)
56	- LLM output stored in knowledge bases or vector DBs without sanitization — stored prompt injection risk
57	
58	#### Shell Injection (Python-specific)
59	- `subprocess.run()` / `subprocess.call()` / `subprocess.Popen()` with `shell=True` AND f-string/`.format()` interpolation in the command string — use argument arrays instead
60	- `os.system()` with variable interpolation — replace with `subprocess.run()` using argument arrays
61	- `eval()` / `exec()` on LLM-generated code without sandboxing
62	
63	#### Enum & Value Completeness
64	When the diff introduces a new enum value, status string, tier name, or type constant:
65	- **Trace it through every consumer.** Read (don't just grep — READ) each file that switches on, filters by, or displays that value. If any consumer doesn't handle the new value, flag it. Common miss: adding a value to the frontend dropdown but the backend model/compute method doesn't persist it.
66	- **Check allowlists/filter arrays.** Search for arrays or `%w[]` lists containing sibling values (e.g., if adding "revise" to tiers, find every `%w[quick lfg mega]` and verify "revise" is included where needed).
67	- **Check `case`/`if-elsif` chains.** If existing code branches on the enum, does the new value fall through to a wrong default?
68	To do this: use Grep to find all references to the sibling values (e.g., grep for "lfg" or "mega" to find all tier consumers). Read each match. This step requires reading code OUTSIDE the diff.
69	
70	### Pass 2 — INFORMATIONAL
71	
72	#### Async/Sync Mixing (Python-specific)
73	- Synchronous `subprocess.run()`, `open()`, `requests.get()` inside `async def` endpoints — blocks the event loop. Use `asyncio.to_thread()`, `aiofiles`, or `httpx.AsyncClient` instead.
74	- `time.sleep()` inside async functions — use `asyncio.sleep()`
75	- Sync DB calls in async context without `run_in_executor()` wrapping
76	
77	#### Column/Field Name Safety
78	- Verify column names in ORM queries (`.select()`, `.eq()`, `.gte()`, `.order()`) against actual DB schema — wrong column names silently return empty results or throw swallowed errors
79	- Check `.get()` calls on query results use the column name that was actually selected
80	- Cross-reference with schema documentation when available
81	
82	#### Dead Code & Consistency (version/changelog only — other items handled by maintainability specialist)
83	- Version mismatch between PR title and VERSION/CHANGELOG files
84	- CHANGELOG entries that describe changes inaccurately (e.g., "changed from X to Y" when X never existed)
85	
86	#### LLM Prompt Issues
87	- 0-indexed lists in prompts (LLMs reliably return 1-indexed)
88	- Prompt text listing available tools/capabilities that don't match what's actually wired up in the `tool_classes`/`tools` array
89	- Word/token limits stated in multiple places that could drift
90	
91	#### Completeness Gaps
92	- Shortcut implementations where the complete version would cost <30 minutes CC time (e.g., partial enum handling, incomplete error paths, missing edge cases that are straightforward to add)
93	- Options presented with only human-team effort estimates — should show both human and CC+gstack time
94	- Test coverage gaps where adding the missing tests is a "lake" not an "ocean" (e.g., missing negative-path tests, missing edge case tests that mirror happy-path structure)
95	- Features implemented at 80-90% when 100% is achievable with modest additional code
96	
97	#### Time Window Safety
98	- Date-key lookups that assume "today" covers 24h — report at 8am PT only sees midnight→8am under today's key
99	- Mismatched time windows between related features — one uses hourly buckets, another uses daily keys for the same data
100	
101	#### Type Coercion at Boundaries
102	- Values crossing Ruby→JSON→JS boundaries where type could change (numeric vs string) — hash/digest inputs must normalize types
103	- Hash/digest inputs that don't call `.to_s` or equivalent before serialization — `{ cores: 8 }` vs `{ cores: "8" }` produce different hashes
104	
105	#### View/Frontend
106	- Inline `<style>` blocks in partials (re-parsed every render)
107	- O(n*m) lookups in views (`Array#find` in a loop instead of `index_by` hash)
108	- Ruby-side `.select{}` filtering on DB results that could be a `WHERE` clause (unless intentionally avoiding leading-wildcard `LIKE`)
109	
110	#### Distribution & CI/CD Pipeline
111	- CI/CD workflow changes (`.github/workflows/`): verify build tool versions match project requirements, artifact names/paths are correct, secrets use `${{ secrets.X }}` not hardcoded values
112	- New artifact types (CLI binary, library, package): verify a publish/release workflow exists and targets correct platforms
113	- Cross-platform builds: verify CI matrix covers all target OS/arch combinations, or documents which are untested
114	- Version tag format consistency: `v1.2.3` vs `1.2.3` — must match across VERSION file, git tags, and publish scripts
115	- Publish step idempotency: re-running the publish workflow should not fail (e.g., `gh release delete` before `gh release create`)
116	
117	**DO NOT flag:**
118	- Web services with existing auto-deploy pipelines (Docker build + K8s deploy)
119	- Internal tools not distributed outside the team
120	- Test-only CI changes (adding test steps, not publish steps)

146	## Fix-First Heuristic
147	
148	This heuristic is referenced by both `/review` and `/ship`. It determines whether
149	the agent auto-fixes a finding or asks the user.
150	
151	```
152	AUTO-FIX (agent fixes without asking):     ASK (needs human judgment):
153	├─ Dead code / unused variables            ├─ Security (auth, XSS, injection)
154	├─ N+1 queries (missing eager loading)      ├─ Race conditions
155	├─ Stale comments contradicting code       ├─ Design decisions
156	├─ Magic numbers → named constants         ├─ Large fixes (>20 lines)
157	├─ Missing LLM output validation           ├─ Enum completeness
158	├─ Version/path mismatches                 ├─ Removing functionality
159	├─ Variables assigned but never read       └─ Anything changing user-visible
160	└─ Inline styles, O(n*m) view lookups        behavior
161	```
162	
163	**Rule of thumb:** If the fix is mechanical and a senior engineer would apply it
164	without discussion, it's AUTO-FIX. If reasonable engineers could disagree about
165	the fix, it's ASK.
166	
167	**Critical findings default toward ASK** (they're inherently riskier).
168	**Informational findings default toward AUTO-FIX** (they're more mechanical).
